What’s Happening in Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte’s Impeachment Trial?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:45:00 UTC
06:45:00 KST

This week marks the second month of the impeachment trial of Philippine Vice President Sara Duterte, who is accused of betrayal of public trust over the alleged misuse of public funds, accumulation of unexplained wealth, and making grave threats against the president. What has happened over the past two months, and what’s the prospect of her conviction or acquittal?
Two articles of the impeachment complaint have been presented already to the public. The first accusation refers to her involvement in a conspiracy to assassinate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The second issue, which is considered by anti-corruption advocates as the main aspect of the case, is about Duterte’s anomalous spending of confidential funds.
Perhaps the prosecution decided to prioritize the presentation of the issue of grave threats to galvanize and unite the president’s constituency. The evidence was clear even if Duterte’s camp tried hard to undermine the testimony of the witnesses from law enforcement bodies. Duterte’s defense tactic is expected to double down on the argument about the vice president exercising her freedom of speech.
As expected, the confidential funds issue has produced old and new documentary evidence showing the irregular spending of Duterte’s office. The prosecution is not yet done presenting the case, and they could follow this up by highlighting the suspicious bank transactions made by Duterte and her husband. Based on the line of questioning and earlier manifestations of Duterte’s legal team, they could try to link the questionable use of funds to the counterinsurgency operations of security forces. They could also assert the inadmissibility of evidence by citing bank secrecy laws.
Duterte is not required to appear at the trial, but she has been called out for her absence while disparaging her accusers in her public appearances. In particular, she has lambasted prosecutors for “fishing for evidence” and concocting “wild stories” of alleged wrongdoing. The defense panel has also criticized some prosecutors for posting offensive remarks on social media.
The impeachment is more than just a legal process; it is a political mechanism designed to hold officials accountable. A vicious exchange of political rhetoric from both parties and other stakeholders is intended to gather public support. Nevertheless, the presiding officer issued a ruling that prohibited all those directly involved in the trial from commenting about the case. The ruling covers Duterte, which might restrict her ability to argue her case and influence public opinion.
After two months, there have been suggestions to shorten the duration of the trial. The prosecution is studying the option of foregoing the presentation of other articles of impeachment since they believe they have already made a solid case for the conviction of Duterte. It could also mean that they wanted to expedite the trial to sustain public interest. A crucial decision point is the legal assertion by some lawmakers to lower the number of votes required to convict Duterte, since some senator-judges have been unable to participate in the proceedings because they have been detained over corruption charges. Another senator-judge has left the country and is reportedly seeking medical treatment. This legal question could reach the Supreme Court and potentially make a huge impact on the case and the country’s politics ahead of the 2028 elections.
Contrary to initial impressions, it is not impeachment matters that have dominated recent political debates but the unresolved corruption controversies and the massive flooding that hit vast areas of Luzon, the country’s biggest island. This was less because the impeachment was less interesting than the fact that residents had to prioritize survival amid rising floodwaters and point out the continuing failure to hold accountable the corrupt officials implicated in the infrastructure scam. It didn’t help that the draft budget bill for 2027 retained fund items that can be used for political patronage and pork barrel distribution.
As the nation marks the first anniversary of last year’s widespread anti-corruption protests, residents in flooded communities are joined by concerned citizens who are outraged over the continuing impunity and the apparent failure or reluctance of the Marcos government to overhaul the budget system that enabled the systematic stealing of the country’s resources.
Duterte might try to echo the public discontent against the entrenched corruption in the bureaucracy to divert attention from her trial, but she has no credibility in leading the advocacy for good governance. She is a target of the citizen-led anti-corruption movement, which is demanding accountability from the country’s two highest officials.
The impeachment could soon end before the end of the year, and the supposedly transparent and inclusive 2027 budget bill may be enacted into law on time; but as things stand today, the struggle to end corruption could take much longer.

High Court dismisses petition by expatriates seeking to vote in upcoming election
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:43:38 UTC
06:43:38 KST

Israel’s High Court on Wednesday dismissed a petition by Israeli expatriates seeking to vote in the October 27 election after discovering that they had been excluded from the voter rolls under a little-known Interior Ministry classification that records certain citizens as nonresidents.
The petition was filed by some 100 expatriate Israelis challenging their exclusion from the voter rolls under an Interior Ministry classification known as “Code 51,” which records them as having ceased to be Israeli residents.
The petitioners said they had never asked to give up their status as Israeli residents and questioned the legal authority, criteria, and process by which the classification was imposed. Some only discovered the designation when they checked their eligibility ahead of the election.
The court did not resolve that factual dispute, instead dismissing the petition on procedural grounds. Justice Yechiel Kasher said the case was filed too late, a week before the voter registry was due to be finalized, and that the petitioners had not first used the statutory appeals process available to challenge their registration status. The court also said the petition lacked a detailed factual record showing how each of the petitioners came to receive Code 51.
The case arose as tens of thousands of Israeli citizens living abroad are making plans to return to Israel to cast ballots in the country’s first national election since the October 7 Hamas attack. More than 30,000 expatriates had registered with Fly&Vote, an initiative helping Israelis arrange election travel, which has already secured seven dedicated flights to Israel.
The Interior Ministry told the court that Code 51 is given to citizens who informed a population registry official that they were leaving Israel and asked not to remain registered as residents. The petitioners disputed that account, saying they had never asked for their registration as Israeli residents to be canceled.
Israeli informed of change to residency status while registering newborn son
Ilana Mittman, a retired social scientist living in Baltimore and a petitioner in the case, discovered this summer that her residency status had been changed under Code 51 on March 7, 1986, the same date she visited the Israeli Consulate in San Francisco to register her newborn son.
Mittman told the Jewish Telegraphic Agency that consular staff took away her Israeli ID card during the 1986 appointment without explanation. “I remember how bad of a feeling it was to give that document away,” she said. “I felt I gave a part of myself away when that happened. But I didn’t know that my biggest right as a citizen – the right to vote – was just robbed from me.”
The petition also challenged the law tying voting eligibility to residency, arguing that it conflicts with Israel’s Basic Law governing the Knesset, which guarantees every Israeli citizen aged 18 or older the right to vote unless a court has deprived them of that right. The court did not decide that question, and Kasher said the petitioners could raise it again after the election.

Israeli filmmaker Guy Nattiv’s new film, The Liberation, had its world premiere on September 4 at the prestigious Telluride Film Festival in Colorado.
It will have its Canadian premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival, which runs September 10-20.
The psychological drama, written by Nattiv and Noa Berman-Herzberg, was inspired by a true story from Nattiv’s family.
It centers on Rita, a character based on his Holocaust-survivor grandmother, who falls under the spell of a charismatic cult leader and leaves her family to join an isolated women’s commune.
When Rita’s daughters unexpectedly arrive to convince her to come home, they too are drawn into the cult’s manipulative and emotionally charged world, forcing Rita to choose between the new life she has embraced and the family she left behind.
Nattiv is no stranger to film awards and festivals
Nattiv’s previous films include Tatami, a portrait of female Iranian judokas at odds with the Iranian regime; Golda, a drama starring Helen Mirren about Golda Meir during the Yom Kippur War; and the feature-length movie about an American skinhead, Skin, starring Jamie Bell, and the Oscar-winning short film of the same name.
In The Liberation, Nattiv has assembled a high-profile cast. Carrie Coon (The White Lotus, The Gilded Age) stars as Rita, with Bella Ramsey (The Last of Us) and Odessa Young (Mothering Sunday) playing her daughters.
Lily James (Mamma Mia! Here We Go Again, and Cinderella) portrays the cult leader, while actor and playwright Tracy Letts, Coon’s husband in real life, plays her husband onscreen.
Jaime Ray Newman, Nattiv’s wife and longtime producing partner, also appears in the film.
The film, originally titled Harmony, was announced as part of Telluride’s lineup on September 3, in keeping with the festival’s tradition of keeping its tightly curated program secret until just before opening day.

AfD wants to form a government in Saxony-Anhalt — but how?
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:41:00 UTC
06:41:00 KST

Can the AfD form a government in Saxony-Anhalt?
September 7, 2026
The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) achieved its best-ever election result in the state election in Saxony-Anhalt, winning well over 40% of the vote and leaving all other parties far behind.
However, the party lacks the majority of seats in parliament needed to govern on its own. Because the AfD in Saxony-Anhalt has been classified as "confirmed far-right extremist" by the domestic intelligence agency, other parties announced that cooperation with the AfD was out of the question. This will make forming a government in this eastern German state quite difficult.
On election night, Ulrich Siegmund announced on public broadcaster ARD: "As a democrat, I will reach out to all those who wish to work with us to bring about a fundamental political turnaround." At the same time, he acknowledged that there are currently no political parties that he considers suitable for a coalition government.
Above all, he was referring to the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU), which currently holds power in coalitions both in Saxony-Anhalt and on the federal level in Germany. Siegmund, along with the entire AfD leadership, has characterized the CDU's policy of refusing to work with the AfD a failure.
On public broadcaster ZDF, AfD party co-leader Alice Weidel sharply criticized the CDU for stonewalling the AfD: "The CDU will not win another election — not a federal election. And this clearly gives the AfD a mandate to govern. Because we are democrats, we do not refuse to work with others."
On election night, Ulrich Siegmund emphasized that implementing the AfD's platform was more important to him than the prospect of power: "There will be no compromise with me." Leading up to the vote, the 35-year-old AfD lead candidate repeatedly stated that he was only interested in governing alone in order to usher in a fundamental political change in Germany.
The AfD's radical governing platform
For months, the AfD's political program has sparked heated debates across Germany. That's because the party wants to drastically tighten asylum and immigration policies. It wants to speed up the deportation of illegal asylum seekers and introduce a general work requirement for all other asylum seekers.
Above all, however, it wants to make Saxony-Anhalt and Germany less attractive to immigrants and is calling for a "180-degree turnaround in migration policy." During its election campaign, the party repeatedly blamed migrants for crime in German cities and for the housing shortage.
What's more, the AfD is planning a radical restructuring of society: it has declared war on public broadcasting, wants to cut funding for democracy projects, intends to establish a kind of vigilante group against migrants and aims to combat social diversity — all of which is laid out in its platform. And Ulrich Siegmund emphasized in an ARD interview that these issues are non-negotiable.
Now, one option involves a minority government led by the AfD, in which it would need to secure support from other parties to advance its policies.
AfD Chairwoman Alice Weidel told ZDF television: "Who ultimately forms the government — perhaps through a tolerance agreement or even a coalition — remains to be seen."
On behalf of the CDU, the party's secretary-general, Franziska Hoppermann, categorically ruled out a coalition: "There will be no cooperation with the far left or the far right."
Could the BSW help the AfD form a government?
The biggest unknown in this power struggle is the Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW), should it manage to move into the state parliament.
The small party campaigns primarily on a left-wing economic platform and — similar to the AfD — calls for a foreign policy that is more friendly toward Russia. In the past, party founder and former member of the socialist Left Party, Sahra Wagenknecht, has repeatedly expressed openness to substantive cooperation with the AfD. However, for ideological reasons, the party is not considered a particularly attractive partner within AfD circles.
As the AfD celebrated its victory into the night and even before the vote count was complete, some AfD state politicians announced that, if necessary, they intended to remain in the opposition and keep the other parties on the defensive until they could secure a majority of their own.
Take, for example, Oliver Kirchner, co-chair of the AfD caucus in the state parliament of Saxony-Anhalt: "If we end up behind the lectern as the opposition, it will be brutal for the others," he warned during an AfD livestream.
This article has been translated from German.

5 poll-bound states set to vote in February-March
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:40:14 UTC
06:40:14 KST

NEW DELHI: The advancement of Census in the four poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa - coupled with deferment of first phase of Census in the fifth poll-bound state of Manipur - has essentially cemented the schedule for the next round of assembly elections in the five states to Feb-March next year.Among the five states, the term of the Manipur assembly is expiring the earliest - on March 13, 2027. The term of Goa assembly ends March 14, 2027; Punjab assembly on March 16; Uttarakhand on March 28; and Uttar Pradesh only on May 22. All five had gone to polls together in 2022, but the first sitting of the UP assembly was on May 22, 2022.Since 2027 polls in these states will also be simultaneous, Election Commission is likely to take the conventional route of winding up polls before the earliest assembly expiry date - March 13.
UP will vote almost 2 months before House term expires
Thus, the UP polls would be held almost two months before the date of expiry of its assembly. This is in keeping with the pattern of the last three polls. EC's constitutional mandate allows it to hold a state poll anytime within six months prior to the expiry of its assembly's term.Given that a large and populous state like UP is almost certain to have multi-phase polling - though with fewer phases, going by the precedent set by EC in Bihar and West Bengal - polling could start in Feb or even in the beginning of March in case EC decides to restrict polls to two phases, like in Bihar.
The poll announcement may come in Jan 2027.Since SIR has already been completed in three poll-bound states and is under way in the other two, EC is unlikely to go for annual summary revision there ahead of announcing assembly polls. At the end of SIR, the electorate in UP stood at 13.4 crore (decline of 13.2%), in Goa 10.6 lakh (10.2% less) and in Manipur 19.3 lakh (7.6% fall). The final rolls for Punjab and Uttarakhand will be published over the next couple of months.
Centre had yesterday notified its decision to advance the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand and Goa, to the period between Dec 1, 2026, and Jan 4, 2027, with Jan 5 as the reference date. It also notified the deferment of the houselisting phase of Census in Manipur.The advancing of the population enumeration phase in the four other poll-bound states will avert the logistical challenges that would have arisen on account of a clash between the usual timeline for Census and the assembly elections. Both elections and Census rely on the same pool of govt employees - largely teachers - for their conduct.Conventionally, the second phase of Census is held countrywide in Feb, with March 1 as the reference date.

Having covered the Union home ministry, security agencies, Election Commission and the ‘prime’ political beat, the Congress, for The Economic Times all these years, she moved to TOI in August 2012. Her repertoire of news stories delves into the whole gamut of issues related to terrorism and internal strife, besides probing strategic affairs in India’s neighbourhood.

Qantas flight makes priority landing after engine issue sparks panic over New Zealand
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:39:34 UTC
06:39:34 KST

in brief
- Passengers described a terrifying ordeal after flames and loud bangs were seen coming from the left engine of the plane.
- The Boeing 737 landed safely in Christchurch, where emergency crews were waiting.
Emergency services were called to the tarmac when a Qantas flight made a priority landing in Christchurch after an engine issue, which one passenger described as "traumatic".
Liza-Jayne Loch was returning home from a business trip to New Zealand when the Qantas flight ran into trouble.
The plane was climbing above the scenic South Island's mountain ranges on Saturday afternoon, bound for Sydney, when a bang shook the cabin.
A passenger seated nearest the left wing soon shouted, "the engine's on fire", Loch recalled, as the cabin lights began to flicker.
Footage recorded by a passenger and shared with AAP shows flames appearing to issue from the plane's left engine in a series of rapid bursts.
News that makes sense
Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.
"I was sitting on the left-hand side of the plane, and the flames were very, very visible," Loch said.
"There was a lot of screaming at the time."
As the plane continued to gain altitude, Loch tried to comfort herself by recalling that modern jets could land safely on a single engine.
"That's what I kept in my head, that we could actually fly on one engine," she said.
"But the flames kept coming and the noise kept coming."
QF122 suffered a suspected engine issue shortly after taking off from Queenstown on Saturday afternoon, before making a priority landing at Christchurch.
According to Flight Aware, the Boeing 737 landed about 52 minutes after take-off, touching down shortly before 5pm local time.
The cause of the incident has yet to be determined, but Qantas sent two engineers to Christchurch on Sunday to investigate.
Both engines are thought to have remained in operation for the duration of the flight.
Loch said conditions soon stabilised after the initial shock, while cabin staff took pains to comfort passengers.
"The crew were all terribly, terribly calming," Loch said.
'Massive cheers'
Emergency services were waiting on the tarmac when the flight landed, and passengers were allowed to disembark as normal after a short wait.
"There were massive cheers when we landed," Loch said.
A Qantas spokesperson said the plane was believed to have suffered an engine issue and steps would be taken to support affected customers.
"Our pilots are highly trained to manage situations like this and the aircraft landed safely," they said.
"We know this would have been a distressing experience for passengers and will be contacting all customers to provide support."
Affected passengers were put up in a hotel near the Christchurch International Airport before being booked on a complimentary flight to Sydney on Sunday.
While the second flight went off without a hitch, Loch said nerves were still high.
"I cried getting off the plane when we landed in Sydney," Loch said.
"It was quite traumatic."

Hundreds of far-right protesters descend on Portsmouth after small boat arrival
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:38:52 UTC
06:38:52 KST

Hundreds of far-right activists have descended on Portsmouth, where a small boat with 140 asylum seekers on board was intercepted heading towards the Portsmouth coast. The vessel’s arrival sparked a major response with a helicopter, an aeroplane and lifeboats sent to the scene.
It is thought to be the first time such a large boat containing asylum seekers has been brought to Portsmouth and the first time a large group of anti-migrant protesters have tried to block newly arrived asylum seekers from being processed.
The protesters blocked roads for hours and had vowed to stay all night to prevent the new arrivals from being taken to a processing centre. The demonstration ended about 3am, when police obtained a dispersal order and threatened arrests.
It is the second major anti-migrant protest of the weekend. Many of those at Portsmouth were dressed in all black and wore face masks, similar to those who attended a rally that blocked roads in Dover on Saturday.
One witness who was not involved in the protest said on Sunday night: “The atmosphere here is still very tense. The coaches carrying asylum seekers have still not left. About 25-30% of the far-right protesters are wearing balaclavas and many are wearing black. Two police cars had their windscreens smashed by protesters. At one point they broke through the police cordon.”
The boat’s occupants were brought to shore in the maritime city and the Home Office’s plan was to take them to Manston, outside Ramsgate in Kent, where small boat arrivals are processed.
However, videos circulating on social media showed large groups of protesters close to the coaches that were to be used, with some blocking vehicles carrying asylum seekers from leaving.
Late on Sunday, Hampshire police had urged people to avoid the area, and said a dispersal order was in place.
The government has condemned what it described as the “thuggish behaviour” of the protesters. “We condemn the intimidating and thuggish behaviour we are seeing tonight,” a government spokesperson said. “The right to peaceful protest is fundamental to our democracy, but it must never cross a line into disorder.”
In a livestream from the scene, Daniel Thomas, also known as Danny Tommo – a former bodyguard of the far-right activist Tommy Robinson, whose real name is Stephen Yaxley-Lennon – encouraged viewers to travel to Portsmouth to join the protest.
Thomas has recently established Patriot Platform which blocked part of port of Dover on Saturday. He previously launched Operation Overlord which planned to send far-right activists to France to “stop the boats”. He and his supporters filmed themselves slashing abandoned dinghies on a French beach. The french authorities subsequently banned him from France.
Small boat crossings so far this year have reduced by more than 40% compared with the same period last year. While the Home Office has disrupted the smugglers’ business model, their methods appear to have evolved by launching boats such as the one that arrived on Sunday evening from different parts of the coast, much further from the UK, making the crossings more dangerous.
Most small boat arrivals are rescued by Border Force and RNLI boats on the English side of the Channel and brought ashore in Dover.
The Maritime and Coastguard Agency said it was alerted on Sunday to a small boat heading towards the Hampshire coast. The coastguard sent lifeboats, a helicopter, an aeroplane and rescue teams to the area, a spokesperson said. “Border Force, Border Security Command, Hampshire police and south central ambulance service were also sent,” they said.
Saturday’s Port of Dover rally was criticised by politicians from all parties, with questions expected to be raised on Monday about whether Kent police were prepared for it. There could be similar criticism of Hampshire police.
The Dover demonstrations brought traffic on routes to the UK’s busiest international ferry and passenger port to a halt, delaying some ferry services and blocking major roads, but there were no arrests.
The business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, criticised the demonstrations, which saw protesters march through Dover chanting “Whose streets? Our streets” and “Stop the boats”.
Reynolds told Sky News he condemned the behaviour and the disruption it caused, adding: “Peaceful protest – essential part of British life, but that’s not dressing up in costumes like this and disrupting people’s lives.”
On Sunday night, a Home Office spokesperson said: “This government is bearing down on dangerous small boat crossings and restoring control at our border. Joint efforts have seen over 48,000 crossing attempts prevented and 1,100 boats and engines seized since the election.
“We are making progress, with the number of small boat crossings down this year and the lowest number recorded for the month of July since 2020.
“But we must go further, which is why we have signed a payment-by-results deal with the French to put 40% more boots on the ground on French beaches.”

Breast milk shows benefit against antibiotic resistance
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:30:56 UTC
06:30:56 KST

A CSIC-led study finds that certain components of breast milk are linked to fewer antibiotic-resistance genes in babies' gut microbiota.
Breast milk may offer babies a new health benefit: helping to limit the presence of antibiotic resistance genes in their gut. That is the conclusion of an international study led by Spain's National Research Council (CSIC), which has examined how certain components of human milk influence the bacteria that colonise the gut during the first months of life.
The study, published in "Cell Reports Medicine (source in Spanish)", finds that exclusive breastfeeding is associated with a lower abundance and diversity of antimicrobial resistance genes in babies' intestines.
"Promoting breastfeeding appears to be an effective strategy for reducing antimicrobial resistance genes present in intestinal bacterial communities during a critical stage in the development of the microbiota", explains M. Carmen Collado, a CSIC researcher at the Institute of Agrochemistry and Food Technology (IATA).
How does breast milk influence antibiotic resistance?
One of the keys lies in human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), molecules that occur naturally in breast milk which babies do not digest directly, but which serve as food for certain beneficial gut bacteria and help maintain a balanced microbiota.
The researchers have found that some of these components are associated with a lower presence of certain genes conferring resistance to antibiotics.
"HMOs act as ecological modulators of the gut microbiota: they promote the growth of microorganisms capable of using them and may limit the spread of bacteria carrying specific resistance genes", says Collado.
To reach these conclusions, the researchers analysed faecal samples from 57 one-month-old babies in Valencia, along with milk samples from their mothers. The results were later validated with data from another 199 breastfed babies in the Netherlands.
Mode of delivery also plays a role
The study notes that both the mode of delivery and feeding are decisive factors in the composition of the intestinal resistome, that is, the collection of antimicrobial resistance genes present in gut bacteria.
The researchers found differences in the diversity of these genes between babies born by caesarean section and those born by vaginal delivery, while exclusive breastfeeding was associated with a lower abundance and diversity of resistance genes.
"The first months of life represent a critical window in which the gut microbiota is being established and in which different environmental factors, such as mode of delivery or feeding, can leave a lasting imprint", explains Anna Samarra, a researcher trained at IATA-CSIC and now a postdoctoral researcher at the University of California, San Diego.

Heading to America to bridge the gap in US-China relations
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:30:06 UTC
06:30:06 KST

Heading to America to bridge the gap in US-China relations
In a year-long research across America, I hope to map where superpower friction ends, and where shared interest must begin
Before boarding my flight to Boston late last month, I spent the better part of three days doing something I never imagined I would do in more than 30 years of covering China: scrubbing my phone. Old emails, screenshots, WeChat threads that might be read the wrong way, anything that could be misconstrued in an airport interview room – all deleted, just in case.
I was not being paranoid. I was following advice now routinely passed among Chinese travellers to the United States: carry a clean phone, or better yet, a burner. American officials, academics and business travellers headed into China have long been told the same thing. Two sets of citizens, one shared instinct – that what is on your phone could get you into trouble on the other side.
Beginning this month, I take up a one-year appointment as a senior visiting scholar at the Rajawali Foundation Institute for Asia at the Harvard Kennedy School. My purpose is straightforward to state and harder to fulfil: to sit down with American thought leaders across the political spectrum and ask them where they think this relationship is headed, and whether conflict is as inevitable as it now appears.
Layered on top were structural anxieties. In Washington, there is the perceived erosion of American primacy in manufacturing and superpower status. In Beijing, there is a mirror-image worry: that a declining but still-dominant America, unwilling to accept the reality of a rising China, is bent on containing its development, through tariffs, technology export controls and alliances built for that purpose.

China Focus: Think tank report highlights value of China's new popular literature, art
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
05:26:53 CST
06:26:53 KST

An international symposium themed "Consolidate Cultural Subjectivity in Promoting Chinese Modernization" is held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, Sept. 6, 2026. The symposium brought together about 130 experts, scholars and guests from home and abroad. (Xinhua/Mao Siqian)
SHENZHEN, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- New popular literature and art, characterized by broad public participation in the era of the internet and AI, are helping China better express itself and contribute to a fairer global cultural order, according to a think tank report released on Sunday.
Titled "The Flourishing Development and Global Influence of New Popular Literature and Art," the report was issued by the National High-Level Think Tank of Xinhua News Agency at an international symposium held in Shenzhen, a tech hub in south China's Guangdong Province.
The report said new popular literature and art refer to "a brand-new, composite literary and artistic ecosystem that has emerged in the realm of literature and art, driven by the scientific and technological revolution encompassing the internet, big data and AI."
This ecosystem features broad public participation in creation, dissemination and sharing, and reflects the voice of the people and the themes of the times, according to the report.
"Rooted in everyday life, it responds to the aesthetic needs of the people...and is increasingly showcasing Chinese characteristics, style and manner in global cultural exchanges," the report noted.
At a time when globalization and digitalization converge, the report emphasized that new popular literature and art are employing a multiplicity of narratives to shift China's image from one "defined by others" to one "expressed by itself."
They draw on Eastern wisdom to offer a value reference for the shared dilemmas confronting humanity, the report stated. Through openness and collaboration, they help break up the concentrated structure of the global cultural industry. By harnessing technology, they contribute to building a fairer global cultural order.
Themed "Consolidate Cultural Subjectivity in Promoting Chinese Modernization," the symposium brought together about 130 experts, scholars and guests from home and abroad.
Hong Dayong, deputy head of the Publicity Department of the CPC Central Committee, said in his opening speech that China's efforts to strengthen its cultural subjectivity have offered insights for countries around the world to preserve their cultural characteristics and identities and explore development paths suited to their own civilizations.
Lyu Yansong, editor-in-chief of Xinhua News Agency, said in his address that Xinhua will further explore new ways of communication and expression, thus enabling countries around the world to gain a deeper understanding of the historical richness, intellectual depth and vitality of Chinese civilization through the vivid practice of Chinese modernization.
Four parallel sessions were held during the symposium, respectively themed "the humanomics in the new era," "promote new forms of literature and art for the general public in the internet age," "deepen exchanges and mutual learning among civilizations," and "build Chinese intellectual system in philosophy and social sciences." ■

"Spider-Man: Brand New Day" tops North American box office for 6th straight weekend
China
Unknown Publisher

LOS ANGELES, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Sony and Marvel's superhero film "Spider-Man: Brand New Day" maintained its reign at the North American box office, adding 18 million U.S. dollars during its sixth weekend of release for a domestic tally of 917.76 million dollars through Sunday, according to data released by measurement firm Rentrak.
"Spider-Man: Brand New Day" is the first film since 2022's "Avatar: The Way of Water" to top the North American box office for six consecutive weekends. The film, based on the Marvel Comics character Spider-Man and starring Tom Holland in the titular role, has grossed 2.4 billion dollars worldwide.
Universal Pictures' epic action film "The Odyssey" has likewise demonstrated its staying power at the box office. The film came in second in its eighth weekend, grossing 13 million dollars and bringing its cumulative North American total to 584.8 million dollars.
Rounding out the top three, Ketchup Entertainment's live-action animated comedy "Coyote vs. Acme" earned 11.3 million dollars in its second weekend for a domestic cume of 33.8 million dollars. ■

====================================================================================================

Economic Watch: Eight central financial enterprises unveil plans to bolster capital, support economy
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
05:26:49 CST
06:26:49 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Eight central financial enterprises, including the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC), on Sunday unveiled plans to replenish capital, with the funds to strengthen their core Tier 1 capital.
The eight enterprises are set to raise or receive a combined 360 billion yuan (about 53.11 billion U.S. dollars).
Experts said the capital replenishment is a forward-looking policy measure that is expected to further strengthen the financial institutions' sound operations, enhance their ability to withstand risks, and improve their capacity to serve the real economy.
Agricultural Bank of China (ABC) and the ICBC announced plans to raise up to a combined 260 billion yuan through A-share issuances to designated investors to replenish their core Tier 1 capital.
ABC said in a filing with the Shanghai Stock Exchange that it plans to issue A-shares to China's Ministry of Finance (MOF), China National Tobacco Corporation and its relevant subsidiaries, with total proceeds of up to 160 billion yuan.
After deducting issuance expenses, the bank will use all proceeds to replenish its core Tier 1 capital. The final fundraising amount will depend on the issuance plan approved by regulatory authorities, according to ABC.
ICBC said separately that it plans to raise up to 100 billion yuan via an A-share issuance to the MOF, China National Tobacco Corporation and related subsidiaries.
The bank said it will use the net proceeds entirely to replenish its core Tier 1 capital. The capital increase will be implemented after the bank completes the required internal and external approval procedures.
Core Tier 1 capital, the highest-quality form of bank capital used to absorb losses, serves as a key buffer against financial risks. If a bank raises more core Tier 1 capital, it generally has more room to expand lending while maintaining regulatory capital ratios.
Also on Sunday, the Export-Import Bank of China said the MOF will inject 30 billion yuan into the bank to better support its policy-finance mandate and service major national strategies, while China Export & Credit Insurance Corporation said it will receive an injection of 10 billion yuan.
China's finance ministry will also provide fresh capital to four major Chinese insurers in moves aimed at strengthening their capital positions, solvency and risk resilience, according to statements released Sunday.
The planned capital replenishment comes as China has been moving to strengthen the capital base of major state-owned financial institutions. The MOF announced in August that it would issue 300 billion yuan of special treasury bonds to support the capital replenishment.
"Financing demands in areas such as technological innovation, industrial upgrading and expanding domestic demand remain strong, requiring stable support from the financial institutions," said Yu Xiang, chief analyst of policy research at CITIC Securities.
The capital replenishment is not simply about "refueling" financial institutions, but about strengthening their capital base to better serve the real economy, Yu said.
The replenishment is also expected to strengthen the risk resilience of central financial enterprises, thereby fostering a stable financial environment for economic development during the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), experts said.
The latest capital replenishment follows a similar move last year. The MOF issued 500 billion yuan in special treasury bonds in 2025 to support the capital replenishment of major state-owned commercial banks.
Compared with last year's measure, the scope of institutions covered by the latest capital increase has been expanded to include policy financial institutions and state-owned commercial insurers.
"The broader scope of the capital increase reflects the different roles of various types of financial institutions. With diversified funding sources, they can work in concert to provide stronger support for the real economy," Yu said. ■

====================================================================================================

China Focus: China's top grain-producing province turns paddies into tourist destinations
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
05:26:45 CST
06:26:45 KST

This photo taken on July 29, 2026 shows a panoramic view of rice paddy art pieces at a rice park in Fujin City, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. (Xinhua)
HARBIN, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Surrounded by four rice paddy art pieces stretching across the vast fields in northeast China, a giant piece in the form of a QR code catches many people's attention. It can be scanned to access an online store for agricultural products.
These art pieces, spanning 120,000 square meters, are located in a rice park in the city of Fujin, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. Heilongjiang, China's top grain-producing province, has transformed vast paddies into thriving tourism destinations, boosting local incomes.
Turning a design into a giant field canvas requires multiple steps, including design, positioning, layout marking and transplanting. Rice varieties are selected to match the palette: black rice for black and brown sections, edible rice for green, and ornamental rice for yellow and white.
However, this form of art was far less precise in its early days.
"When we first tried in 2017, field positioning relied entirely on manual labor. Workers even had to stand high with megaphones to direct the placement," said Wang Chao, head of the office at the Fujin Tourism Development Service Center.
"The designs were mostly flat. Now, GPS positioning and 3D composition techniques have made the lines and layers much sharper," Wang noted.
This rice landscape is drawing growing numbers of visitors.
Zhao Zihan, a tourist from the neighboring city of Shuangyashan, visited the spot in Fujin with her family on a Saturday. "I've passed by several times but never had the chance to stop. This time I came specifically to see it," she said. "The vast rice paddy art lifts my spirit and fills me with hope for the future."
Beyond admiring the scene, visitors can now engage in increasingly diverse and immersive experiences, from transplanting rice and milling grain to exploring rice growth and camping beside the paddies.
Many of the park's service staff come from surrounding villages, and the visitor flow has spurred the growth of nearby farmstay restaurants. Wang said related services earn participating villagers across 10 villages an extra 4,000 yuan (about 590 U.S. dollars) per person each year.
The story of agritourism is unfolding across Heilongjiang's vast landscape.
In Xinghuo Village, a Korean ethnic village in Huachuan County, the transformation is vivid.
Home to 407 households and over 7,400 mu (around 493 hectares) of farmland, the village sits beside a highway amid scenic surroundings, yet was once just an ordinary village focused on rice cultivation.
"Back then, the roads were mostly dirt paths. There was no work for me in the village, so I had to go out and make my way," said Han Liuhua, 45, who left for cities like Shanghai and Qingdao, both in east China, at age 18.
In 2018, she gave up her urban career and returned to the village, becoming the first migrant worker to come back in over 20 years.
"When I first opened the restaurant in 2022, the villagers weren't very optimistic about me. Visitor numbers were low back then," Han said, noting that the scenic area has since brought a surge in foot traffic, and the restaurant's daily sales can now reach more than 16,000 yuan.
"The distance from my office to my restaurant is less than 50 meters. But when tourists are at their peak, it takes me five minutes just to squeeze through," Han said. "I'm one of the biggest beneficiaries of the village's transformation."
In 2025, the village's scenic area opened, welcoming 1.33 million visitors, generating 300 million yuan in revenue across the full industrial chain, and creating jobs for over 800 people.
The scenic area has renovated farmhouse exteriors in the traditional Korean style, built ecological picking gardens, and created an 8,000-square-meter giant rice paddy art piece to develop diversified, immersive and year-round products.
Inside the park, visitors can immerse themselves in Korean ethnic culture and agricultural experiences, from making kimchi and brewing rice wine to transplanting and harvesting rice.
The same trend is unfolding elsewhere in the province. In the city of Wuchang, a renowned rice-growing area, local enterprises are also actively developing agritourism products.
"I often come here after work. Rice has always been close to my heart, and seeing the vast paddies is far more relaxing than visiting a regular park," said a local resident surnamed Hu, who was picnicking at Qiaofu Dayuan Agricultural Co., Ltd.
The company hosts a variety of rice culture events each year, including rice-planting festivals and harvest ceremonies, while also serving as an experimental education base for primary school students, welcoming tens of thousands of visitors from across the country annually.
"Premium rice isn't just about taste. It is about the experience," said Qiao Wenzhi, head of the company, adding that by combining product customization with experiential value, the premium for their rice has risen by up to 40 percent.
Heilongjiang's broader push for agritourism also comes as China moves to diversify its tourism offerings and cultivate new growth drivers for the industry.
"Developing the multiple functions of agriculture" has been incorporated as a measure in the outline of China's 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030), referring to efforts to ensure food security and supply while integrating agriculture with culture and tourism.
The latest five-year tourism development plan, approved by the State Council and released in July 2026, calls for nurturing new drivers of tourism growth and enriching the supply of high-quality tourism experiences. ■

This photo taken on Sept. 5, 2026 shows a rice paddy art piece at a rice park in Fujin City, northeast China's Heilongjiang Province. (Xinhua/Ji Hang)

TEHRAN, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council Mohsen Rezaei has said that his country would announce a restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz in the coming days and place any ship attempting to transit the area on Tehran's sanctions list.
In an interview with state-run IRIB TV, which was broadcast Sunday night, Rezaei said that the zone would extend from "the line where the U.S. naval blockade begins to the Strait of Hormuz region and inside the Persian Gulf on the other side (of the strait)."
Ships that enter the zone without coordination with Iran, he added, would face sanctions affecting their insurance coverage and future passage through the waterway.
Rezaei framed the move as part of a broader strategic shift in Iran's approach to war and diplomacy, aiming at increasing pressure on Washington.
The security official stressed that the Strait of Hormuz is completely closed, dismissing the U.S. claim that ships and oil tankers are crossing the waterway as a "lie."
While acknowledging that some vessels attempt to cross the strait via a route near Oman, often switching off their navigation systems to evade detection, Rezaei said most of those ships "receive blows."
Yet he added that Iran does not intend to sink them for now due to environmental concerns.
Rezaei further revealed that Iran had test-fired for the first time a domestically developed anti-destroyer missile above a U.S. aircraft carrier 48 hours ago, describing it as a warning that the U.S. naval blockade is vulnerable.
"The special missile created a hell for the Americans, and they fled," he said.
Rezaei said the Strait of Hormuz would remain closed unless the United States takes practical steps to fulfill its obligations under a peace memorandum of understanding signed between Tehran and Washington in June.
In the coming days, he added, a new international corridor designated by Iran and Oman for passage through the strait would be announced, emphasizing that the corridor would be under Iran's management.
Following U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran on Feb. 28, Tehran restricted passage through the Strait of Hormuz, while U.S. forces imposed a naval blockade targeting vessels traveling to or from Iranian ports and coastal areas. ■

Valentin Debise of EASTROC ZXMOTO Evan Bros Factory competes during the race 2 of WorldSSP at the FIM Supersport World Championship French Round in Magny-Cours, France, Sept. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Huiwo)
MAGNY-COURS, France, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Chinese motorcycle brands are gaining visibility both on the racetrack and among French enthusiasts, as strong results in international competition coincide with growing consumer interest in one of Europe's major motorcycle markets.
At the FIM Supersport World Championship's French Round, which concluded Sunday at the Nevers Magny-Cours Circuit, riders Valentin Debise and Federico Caricasulo delivered a strong weekend for Chinese manufacturer ZXMOTO and the Evan Bros Racing team.
The pair secured a historic one-two in Friday's Superpole, with home rider Debise taking his first career WorldSSP pole ahead of Caricasulo. They finished third and fifth respectively in Race 1, while Debise claimed another third-place finish and Caricasulo finished eighth in Sunday's Race 2.
Speaking to Xinhua ahead of the race, Debise said ZXMOTO's approach to motorcycle development was one of the reasons he decided to join the fledgling racing project.
"At the beginning, that's what convinced me to join ZXMOTO, because that's what they told me: 'We want to make the best motorcycle. That's what matters,'" Debise said.
The French rider, who made his first trip to China during the recent summer break, said the drive for constant improvement he observed there had strengthened his confidence in the potential of China's motorcycle industry in France and across Europe.
For ZXMOTO, its debut WorldSSP campaign is also part of a broader push into Europe. Huang Qin, head of the company's foreign trade department, said the largely European championship provides a platform to raise its profile in a key overseas market.
In France, ZXMOTO is working with motorcycle importer and distributor DIP. Anthony Barneaud, who oversees the brand at the company, said it had already received "a significant number of pre-orders" ahead of the first deliveries to French dealers.
Valentin Debise of EASTROC ZXMOTO Evan Bros Factory reacts after the race 2 of WorldSSP at the FIM Supersport World Championship French Round in Magny-Cours, France, Sept. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Huiwo)
Barneaud said ZXMOTO's WorldSSP performances had created a "real surprise effect," generating greater interest from riders and dealers. More broadly, he said Chinese brands were gradually changing perceptions by showing French motorcyclists they could offer reliable, well-equipped motorcycles at competitive prices.
Away from the track, Chinese manufacturers were also drawing attention from spectators browsing motorcycle displays around the circuit.
"Chinese motorcycles offer very good value for money," said Ludovic, a French motorcycle enthusiast. A long-time fan of Italian brands, he said Chinese manufacturers had increasingly caught his attention.
Interest is also visible online. The 2026 ZXMOTO 820RR attracted more than 10,000 unique visitors to its model page over the latest quarter on French motorcycle website Motoplanete, making it the site's most-viewed motorcycle model page during the period. The CFMOTO 1000 MT-X 2026, from another Chinese brand, ranked second.
Other Chinese manufacturers were also visible at Magny-Cours. A QJMotor display drew a steady stream of spectators during the weekend.
A staff member from SIMA, QJMotor's importer in France, told Xinhua that Chinese manufacturers' progress in international racing had helped increase their visibility among French riders. "It's important for us," he said.
Valentin Debise (front) of EASTROC ZXMOTO Evan Bros Factory competes during the race 2 of WorldSSP at the FIM Supersport World Championship French Round in Magny-Cours, France, Sept. 6, 2026. (Xinhua/Wu Huiwo)
The interest comes as Chinese motorcycle brands continue to expand their presence in France. In May, they accounted for 15.7 percent of new motorcycle registrations, according to French publication L'Automobile Magazine. Registrations rose 58 percent year-on-year that month, meaning roughly one in six newly registered motorcycles was from a Chinese brand.
Huang said attracting attention through racing and new products was only a first step. Building lasting consumer trust in mature overseas markets would also require competitive products, sustained participation in top-level racing, a strong dealer network and reliable after-sales service.
"Only then can we achieve sales in mature markets and build a strong reputation for the brand," Huang said. ■

A voter arrives at a polling station in Magdeburg, Germany, Sept. 6, 2026. The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has won Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt with a record 44.5 percent of the vote, according to an exit poll released by public broadcaster ARD. (Xinhua/Zhang Haofu)
MAGDEBURG, Germany, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- The far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) has won Sunday's state election in Saxony-Anhalt with a record 44.4 percent of the vote, according to an exit poll released by public broadcaster ARD.
The Christian Democratic Union (CDU), led by incumbent state leader Sven Schulze, suffered a heavy blow, plunging to 18.4 percent, down from 37.1 percent in 2021, the poll showed.
The Left party came in third with 9.3 percent, followed by the Greens with 8.7 percent and the Social Democratic Party (SPD) with 8.4 percent.
The newly formed Sahra Wagenknecht Alliance (BSW) hovered right on the 5-percent threshold to enter the state parliament, while the business-friendly Free Democratic Party (FDP) crashed out with just 2.2 percent.
Conceding defeat, Schulze acknowledged the AfD's clear victory, while urging political leaders across Germany to heed the message sent by voters.
In Berlin, head of the Chancellery Nina Warken called the election outcome a "watershed moment" for the CDU, describing it on broadcaster ZDF as a "very, very difficult result." Warken also insisted that the federal government would resolutely press ahead with its planned reform agenda.
In the 83-seat state parliament, the AfD is projected to secure 39 seats, three seats shy of an absolute majority needed to govern alone.
The AfD's 35-year-old state lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund hailed the result, declaring that "the people have sent a clear signal."
Speaking to ARD, Siegmund also signaled a shift from his pre-election stance of only seeking office through an absolute majority, noting that his party is now open to a coalition.
However, all other mainstream parties have repeatedly ruled out entering a coalition with the AfD. It remains unclear how a viable state government will be formed. ■

But behind efforts to keep schools operating, Palestinian education officials say a deepening financial crisis is placing additional pressure on the education system.
"The new academic year began amid field and financial challenges that have affected various aspects of the educational process," said Sadiq al-Khadour, spokesperson for the Ministry of Education.
Al-Khadour said that the financial crisis had affected the renewal of school furniture, completion of administrative buildings and equipping of some schools.
He attributed the difficulties affecting teachers and students to the financial crisis facing Palestinian Authority institutions and widespread job losses among Palestinians since the outbreak of the latest round of Palestinian-Israeli conflict in October 2023.
For 10-year-old Suleiman Khaled, the economic hardship was reflected in a simple part of the new school year: his school bag.
"I wished I could have a new bag, but my father has been unemployed for almost two years," Khaled said.
The financial burden is also being felt by teachers, who are struggling to meet the educational needs of their own families while continuing to work amid rising living costs.
Palestinian teacher Hussam Aghbaria, 45, from Hebron in the southern West Bank, said the financial difficulties facing teachers had directly affected their daily lives.
Aghbaria, a father of four, including two elementary school students, said rising prices of stationery and school supplies had added pressure on families already facing difficult economic conditions.
"Teachers find themselves in a difficult situation. On the one hand, they have to fulfill their role in teaching students at school, while on the other hand, they have to provide educational supplies for their own children at home amid deteriorating economic conditions," Aghbaria said.
Alongside financial difficulties, students and teachers face daily obstacles in reaching schools, including checkpoints, road closures, military gates and raids.
Al-Khadour said these circumstances were affecting the regularity of education, adding that the ministry had developed alternative plans to help students and teachers reach schools under difficult conditions.
According to a report issued by the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs in April, as of December 2025, the number of movement restrictions imposed on Palestinians in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, reached 925. The figure is 43 percent higher than the annual average of 647 movement obstacles in the preceding 20 years.
Such restrictions have also raised concerns over the ability of students and teachers to reach schools regularly.
Ramallah-based educational expert Youssef Abu Ras said the readiness of schools for the new academic year should not be measured solely by whether they open their doors.
"It should also be measured by the availability and stability of educational conditions and the ability of students and teachers to reach schools and continue their studies regularly," Abu Ras said, adding that the field and financial crises could become permanent rather than exceptional circumstances.
He warned that reduced school hours or disruptions to the academic schedule could negatively affect the future of coming generations. ■

Antonelli storms from 19th to win F1 Italian GP
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-07
05:26:09 CST
06:26:09 KST

By F1 correspondent Michael Butterworth
BEIJING, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- Kimi Antonelli produced a remarkable comeback from 19th on the grid to win his home Italian Grand Prix on Sunday, passing Mercedes teammate George Russell late in a dramatic race at Monza.
Antonelli took the lead for good from Russell at the Ascari chicane on lap 50 after the two Mercedes drivers had traded places repeatedly earlier in the race.
Max Verstappen finished third for Red Bull, ahead of McLaren's Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris, while Lewis Hamilton took sixth for Ferrari.
Antonelli became the first Italian to win his home Grand Prix since Ludovico Scarfiotti in 1966. No Formula One driver had won from as far back as 19th on the grid since John Watson triumphed from 22nd at Long Beach in 1983.
The victory was Antonelli's seventh of the season and extended his championship lead over Russell to 66 points, with Hamilton a further 10 points behind in third.
Mercedes also strengthened its grip on the constructors' championship and now has 468 points, 122 ahead of Ferrari, with McLaren third on 287.
Alpine's Pierre Gasly had claimed a surprise first pole position and initially held off Russell, but the Mercedes driver swept into the lead at the start of lap two.
Moments later, Ferrari's Charles Leclerc crashed heavily at the Parabolica after running wide and losing the rear of his car, causing the race to be halted while barriers were repaired.
Antonelli had already climbed seven places to 12th by the stoppage, which allowed him to discard the hard tires he had started on.
Russell led Gasly and Verstappen at the restart, but Antonelli continued his rapid progress, passing Norris and then Gasly before moving ahead of Hamilton and Piastri to reach third by lap 13.
He caught the leaders soon afterward, beginning a frenetic battle with Russell in which the Mercedes pair repeatedly exchanged first place while Verstappen remained close behind.
Antonelli first took the lead on lap 18 before Russell responded, with the pair trading places several more times as Mercedes attempted to manage their battle.
A virtual safety car following Lance Stroll's retirement on lap 28 changed the complexion of the race. Antonelli and Verstappen pitted while Russell stayed out, leaving Antonelli to fight his way back through traffic.
The Italian quickly dispatched Gasly, Norris, Hamilton and Piastri to return to second and began closing a gap of more than 13 seconds to Russell.
With Russell struggling with tire graining, Antonelli was within striking distance by lap 47. An initial attempt at Turn 1 two laps later sent him briefly through the gravel as Russell defended stoutly, but the Italian recovered before making his decisive move at Ascari on lap 50.
Russell held on for second, with Verstappen third after a race-long battle with Piastri. Norris finished fifth, ahead of Hamilton, Gasly, Arvid Lindblad, Franco Colapinto and Yuki Tsunoda.
The next round of the 2026 season is next weekend's Spanish Grand Prix, which will be held for the first time at the new Madring circuit in Madrid. ■

Once disgraced, twice-resigned, ex-PM Keir Starmer is now ex-MP
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:22:03 UTC
06:22:03 KST

Breadcrumb
Once disgraced, twice-resigned, ex-PM Keir Starmer is now ex-MP
Even in resignation, Keir Starmer is a liability for the Labour Party. One of the most unpopular Prime Ministers in British history, the former Labour leader had transformed an admittedly shallow Parliamentary majority into a succession of by-election defeats, shrinking municipal power, and a perpetual spate of Reform UK polling leads.
Just as Andy Burnham has inaugurated a new period of Labour resurgence by distinguishing himself from his predecessor, operating as a far savvier politician, prioritising Mamdani-style affect and vibes, and even, in a limited way, introducing some cost-of-living reforms, Starmer has caused the new PM a headache by resigning. He will no longer serve as the Parliamentary representative for Holborn and St. Pancras, a seat he has held for eleven years.
Starmer, the man who backed Israel’s genocide of the Palestinians to the hilt and sought to strip the disabled of benefits and pensioners of winter fuel payments, ended his Parliamentary career after six weeks on a summer wage. Putting a damper on Burnham’s hard launch, he also opened himself up to a career that does not involve him declaring his earnings. Starmer’s resignation is a final parting shot to his successor.
This by-election is the first substantive test of the new PM’s wager to rebuild an electoral coalition which binds together significant parts of the Northern electorate with Labour’s disloyal, leftwards-moving voter base in the larger, metropolitan cities.
Starmer’s resignation, as venal and self-obsessed as his time in office, might symbolise a potential challenge to this ambition. Formally, it shouldn’t. The Burnham poll bounce hasn’t been enormous, but it has been significant. He has dragged Labour back to the top from oblivion.
With the opposition in disarray, as Farage faces a litany of financial scandals and Zack Polanski’s Greens struggle to find their feet against a more nimble Labour leader, there is an argument to say that Burnham’s Labour should be commanding far larger polling leads.
There should not be any comfort walking into this by-election, however. The Holborn and St. Pancras constituency, like many London areas, is an almost Dickensian tale of two cities. Sandwiched between London Euston and King's Cross station is the historic working-class Somers Town neighbourhood, just as behind the leafy Victorian and Georgian terraces of Kentish Town and Camden lies a legion of working-class estates.
This seat, in many ways that have been actively papered over in the national political conversation over the past decade, is a classic Labour constituency. It brings together a multiracial working class with a professional middle class that has grown in size both as a component of the area and of Labour’s electoral base.
The Labour Party will hope that the Burnham charm offensive is enough to win the seat, supplementing its superior ground game. Of the Labour candidates on offer, there is a real estate developer, the former leader of Haringey council, and a spate of other councillors in the race. The favourite is likely Sagal Abdi-Wali, the current Camden council leader, former Constituency Labour Party chair, and a Somali refugee.
The New Statesmen’s Ben Walker in a Britain Predicts poll has Labour with a thin 5% lead over the Greens in Starmer’s former constituency. Whilst this is certainly the poll with the most generous tilt towards the eco-populists, the prize for the Greens is clear.
Zack Polanski, who has confidently declared that he will run for the seat so long as he wins the support of the local party, has an opportunity to send a shockwave through London Labour and build upon the Greens’ growing clout across the capital, having won control of five London councils in the recent local elections.
Without the jeopardy of worrying about the seat falling to either the Conservatives or Reform UK, Polanski can confidently claim, as Russell Warfield has argued on PoliticsJOE, that if you want to make good on Andy Burnham’s promise to end neoliberalism, getting another Green into Parliament will be a far better means for making good on that than simply getting another Labour MP elected.
To achieve this, the Greens would need to capitalise on their growing inroads in wards across the constituency whilst also finding firmer footing as they try to pivot against a more capable, Janus-faced Labour leader.
Keir Starmer’s last act as a politician could also be his final gift to the Green Party, handing them an opportunity to regain their momentum and position themselves as the effective opposition to Andy Burnham’s muddied attempt to revive Labour’s fortunes.
Jonas Marvin is the author of forthcoming The Breaking of the English Working Class, due out for Verso Books in August 2026. He also cohosts Life of the Party podcast and blogs at Marx’s Dream Journal.

Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-06
21:21:25 UTC
06:21:25 KST

Popular brain supplement linked to shorter lifespan in men
A common amino acid found in protein-rich foods and supplements may be linked to a shorter lifespan in men.
- Date:
- September 6, 2026
- Source:
- Impact Journals LLC
- Summary:
- A large study involving more than 270,000 people has linked higher blood levels of the amino acid tyrosine to a shorter lifespan in men. Using both observational data and genetic analysis, researchers found that elevated tyrosine could potentially reduce male life expectancy by nearly a year, while no significant effect appeared in women. Tyrosine is found naturally in protein-rich foods and is also sold as a supplement for boosting focus and mental performance, making the finding especially intriguing.
- Share:
A large study involving more than 270,000 people suggests that one common amino acid may be tied to how long men live.
Researchers led by Jie V. Zhao, Yitang Sun, Junmeng Zhang, and Kaixiong Ye from the University of Hong Kong and the University of Georgia examined whether phenylalanine and tyrosine, two amino acids involved in metabolism and brain function, are connected to lifespan (lifespan). Their results point to a notable difference between men and women. Higher tyrosine levels were associated with shorter life expectancy in men, while no significant effect was detected in women.
The findings could eventually help scientists better understand why aging and longevity differ between the sexes, although much more research is needed before the results can be translated into health recommendations.
The research was published in Aging-US titled "The role of phenylalanine and tyrosine in longevity: a cohort and Mendelian randomization study."
Why Tyrosine Matters
Amino acids are the molecular building blocks that the body uses to make proteins. Phenylalanine and tyrosine are both found in foods that contain protein, and they are also available in dietary supplements.
Beyond their role in protein production, these amino acids participate in important biological processes. Tyrosine is especially interesting because the body uses it to produce neurotransmitters such as dopamine. Neurotransmitters are chemical messengers that allow nerve cells to communicate, and dopamine helps regulate functions that include mood, motivation, and thinking.
Despite these important roles, scientists still do not fully understand how long-term differences in phenylalanine and tyrosine levels might influence aging.
More Than 270,000 People Studied
To investigate, the researchers analyzed information from more than 270,000 participants in the UK Biobank, a large research database containing health and genetic data from people in the United Kingdom.
The team used two complementary approaches. First, they looked for associations between blood concentrations of phenylalanine and tyrosine and outcomes related to death and predicted lifespan. They also used genetic methods to investigate whether the relationships might go beyond a simple association.
One of those approaches was Mendelian randomization. This method uses naturally occurring genetic differences among people as a way to test whether a particular biological factor may contribute to an outcome. Because genes are assigned before many lifestyle choices and diseases develop, the technique can sometimes provide stronger clues about cause and effect than an observational study alone.
At first, higher levels of both amino acids appeared to be associated with an increased risk of death. But when the researchers examined the relationships more closely, tyrosine was the one that consistently stood out.
Tyrosine Linked to a Shorter Lifespan in Men
The genetic analyses suggested that elevated tyrosine levels may have a potentially causal relationship with reduced life expectancy in men. According to the researchers' estimates, higher tyrosine could shorten male lifespan by nearly one year.
The same pattern was not seen in women. Researchers found no significant effect of tyrosine on female lifespan.
The relationship also remained after the researchers accounted for phenylalanine and other related factors, strengthening the possibility that tyrosine itself may have an independent connection to aging.
The team also found that men generally have higher levels of tyrosine than women. That difference could potentially contribute to the well-documented gap in average lifespan between the sexes, although the findings do not establish that tyrosine is responsible for that gap.
"Phenylalanine showed no association with lifespan in either men or women after controlling for tyrosine."
Why Might Tyrosine Affect Longevity?
Scientists do not yet know exactly why higher tyrosine levels might be associated with shorter lives in men.
One possible explanation involves insulin resistance. This occurs when cells become less responsive to insulin, the hormone that helps control blood sugar. Insulin resistance is associated with several diseases that become more common with age and could therefore provide one possible link between tyrosine and longevity.
Tyrosine is also used by the body to make neurotransmitters involved in the stress response. Hormones and related signaling pathways can function differently in men and women, which could help explain why the apparent lifespan effect emerged only in men.
These mechanisms remain hypotheses, however, and will require further investigation.
What the Findings Mean for Tyrosine Supplements
Tyrosine is widely sold as a dietary supplement and is often promoted for improving focus, alertness, and mental performance. The new findings therefore raise questions about whether chronically high tyrosine levels could have unintended long-term consequences.
Importantly, the researchers did not directly test tyrosine supplements. The results therefore do not show that taking a tyrosine supplement shortens lifespan.
Instead, the study examined tyrosine levels in the body and their relationship with longevity. The researchers suggest that people with unusually high tyrosine concentrations could potentially benefit from dietary changes designed to lower those levels.
One possible strategy is restricting protein intake, which could reduce tyrosine exposure. However, it remains unclear whether deliberately lowering tyrosine through diet would actually extend lifespan or improve health.
More research will be needed to confirm the results, uncover the biological mechanisms involved, and determine whether diet or lifestyle changes can safely alter tyrosine levels in ways that promote healthier aging.
Story Source:
Materials provided by Impact Journals LLC. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Jie V. Zhao, Yitang Sun, Junmeng Zhang, Kaixiong Ye. The role of phenylalanine and tyrosine in longevity: a cohort and Mendelian randomization study. Aging, 2025; 17 (10): 2500 DOI: 10.18632/aging.206326

Stray US glide bomb likely hit wedding in Iran – WaPo
A US munition likely landed a direct hit on a wedding in Iran last week after it veered off its designated target, the Washington Post reported on Sunday, citing a person familiar with the operation.
The incident occurred in Kuhestak, Hormozgan Province, amid a new wave of airstrikes unleashed by the US on Iran on Tuesday. One of the munitions hit a residential home with a wedding party underway, killing at least five and wounding nearly 70. The Iranian authorities said the victims were three women and two children aged four and 16.
The explosion at the party was highly likely a result of a direct hit by a US munition, according to the WaPo. The US Navy dropped six glide bombs at a communications tower in the town, with all but one striking the designated target. The stray munition missed the tower, reportedly hitting the house located around 135 meters (440 feet) away. The comms tower was the only designated target within the town during the Tuesday strikes, the source told the WaPo, ruling out any prospects the home was attacked intentionally or mixed with some other target.
The reporting is consistent with earlier pieces run by AP, the New York Times, Reuters, and other outlets, which indicated that the wedding party was hit by a US-guided weapon, most likely a JSOW glide bomb, rather than debris or a faulty anti-aircraft missile fired by Iran.
US Vice President J.D. Vance said on Thursday that Washington is looking into the incident. “We’re investigating it because obviously we care. We want to know,” he told reporters. The US military has insisted it does not target civilians and has not taken responsibility for the strike.
The attack on the wedding party has become the latest in the string of civilian mass-casualty incidents that occurred amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
On the opening day of the US-Israeli war on Iran, US forces hit an elementary school in Minab, killing 175 people, predominantly young girls. At least 21 civilians, roughly a third of whom were children, were killed in Lamerd that day. Tehran has repeatedly accused the US of committing war crimes throughout the conflict, reporting some 3,000 civilian casualties since it began late in February.

NEW DELHI: The Centre is in a tangle over Supreme Court's landmark judgement on "creamy layer" that paved the way for induction in the elite civil services of OBC candidates who had cleared the examinations over past ten years but were denied appointments.On Aug 25, govt approached the apex court seeking clarification on the Rohit Nathan judgement that laid down that "salary" could not be added to the "income" to determine if a candidate from a PSU background falls in the "creamy layer" - like it is done for OBCs from non-PSU families. Govt, while seeking that it be allowed to go ahead with allocation of service for Civil Services-2025 without implementing the Nathan judgement, also raised questions about the SC's definition of "creamy layer".But barely a week ago, Centre told Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) that it intended to execute the SC order of March 11. "A decision has been made to implement the decision in terms of the judgement rendered by SC in Union of India vs Rohit Nathan," the ASG told the principal bench of CAT.On Aug 19, CAT was hearing a contempt petition against Centre as an OBC candidate, Basant Singh, had sought that the bench enforce its earlier order for his induction in civil services.
His case was similar to those of candidates in whose favour SC delivered the Nathan judgement."It is further submitted by the learned ASG that 56 similarly placed candidates are also being considered along with the applicant," CAT quoted the ASG as submitting. CAT put off the case based on Centre's undertaking that necessary steps were being taken to implement the Nathan judgement.The apparently contradictory stands taken by govt within a week's interval have disappointed OBC candidates who felt the SC judgement in March had ended their wait for induction in civil services.The case pertains to department of personnel and training (DoPT)'s differential implementation of the "creamy layer" criterion for OBCs from a PSU background and others. While, as per 1993 office memorandum, "salary" and "agricultural income" are not included in computing the "income" of a family, DoPT has been taking "salary" into consideration for candidates with parents in PSUs. Govt has cited the absence of "equivalence of posts" - categorising posts in PSUs, banks, universities, etc.
But, according to guidelines, while Group A and Group B are ineligible for quotas, others are eligible if their "annual income" does not exceed Rs 8 lakh.After a long wait, following orders by three high courts in support of the candidates, SC ruled in March that "salary" cannot be the criterion for determination of "creamy layer" for any category as per the 1993 judgement and that candidates who have suffered should be inducted in civil services.

At least five killed after Amazon cargo plane crash in Miami airport
The cause of the crash is being investigated.
At least five people have died after an Amazon cargo plane crashed in the United States, overrunning its runway while landing at Miami International Airport and disrupting one of the country’s busiest airports.
The US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) said in a social media post that a Boeing 767-300 overran the runway at 2pm ET (18:00 GMT) upon arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico.
